title: moving kids' visits now that I live at the factory

messages.content: ok so im living in the factory now, björn's fault obvs, need to move the kids' visits here!! make it fun so they won't notice the concrete floors. like a treasure hunt but with robots.

Got it! Here's a plan to make the factory visits exciting:

- **Treasure Hunt:** Set up a scavenger hunt using QR codes hidden around the factory. Each code reveals a cool Tusla fact or mini-cipher to decode.
- **Robot Interactions:** Use Optimist robots to guide them through interactive tours. Each stop could have an Optimist performing a fun task or telling a joke.
- **Factory Safari:** Have thematic zones like "Dino Bot Park" with dinosaur-themed machinery covers. Engage them with challenges like spotting the rarest "species."

This blend of exploration, learning, and humor should keep the visits far from bleak. And you can sneak in some quality time amidst production chaos!
perfect!! dino bots are a go!! rex mountain can do a mini fit camp for ‽! one more thing, hide the spreadsheet of doom, don't want them seeing what gary puddle fears most.

Absolutely! We'll tuck the spreadsheet safely away from prying eyes. For additional flair:

- **Fitness Circuit:** Rex Mountain can set up a fun, age-appropriate challenge course using Tusla's gym equipment. Keeps the kids active and entertained!
- **Creative Camouflage:** Decorate the spreadsheet safe as a "Top Secret Lair" room with colorful caution tape, signs, and maybe a flamethrower-themed puzzle lock (just for show).

This way, the kids will have excitement without stumbling upon fiscal fears. Enjoy the family factory fun!
